findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime order keys
findings.body: The new OptimizedCursorPaginator derives keys exactly like Paginator: get_item_key does int(math.floor(value))/math.ceil(value) on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor simply returns cursor.value (an int). It does NOT override these like DateTimePaginator does (which converts a datetime to a float millis value and back). The only caller being added, organization_auditlogs.py, instantiates it with order_by="-datetime", so self.key is "datetime". When build_cursor calls the key on a result whose datetime is a datetime object, math.floor/ceil(datetime) raises TypeError, and build_queryset would also compare the datetime column against an int value_from_cursor. Result: every request that reaches the optimized path (admin + ?optimized_pagination=true) returns a 500. To be usable for datetime ordering this paginator must reuse DateTimePaginator's get_item_key/value_from_cursor.

findings.title: Negative-offset path slices a Django queryset with a negative index and raises
findings.body: The "advanced feature" branch does start_offset = cursor.offset when it is negative, then results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop]). Django querysets do not support negative indices; slicing with a negative start raises AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported."). The inline comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. A client can supply such a cursor because Cursor.from_string parses int(bits[1]) with no sign restriction, so any admin request to the audit-log endpoint with enable_advanced_features=True and a cursor whose offset field is negative will crash. (Same branch also computes the is_prev trimming check as len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the original offset while the slice used start_offset, so the arithmetic is inconsistent when they differ.)

findings.title: Unguarded access to organization_context.member can raise AttributeError
findings.body: enable_advanced is computed as request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional; when it is None (a user with superuser off who reaches this endpoint without a resolved member, e.g. global staff/other access paths) the attribute access raises AttributeError and the endpoint 500s. The value should be derived defensively (e.g. organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access) or the flag should not gate on member at all.

findings.title: Silent span eviction during insert with no metric; max_segment_spans no longer enforced
findings.body: The new eviction (zpopmin set_key, span_count - 1000) silently drops the lowest-score (earliest end_timestamp) spans once a segment exceeds 1000 entries, with no counter/metric to make the loss observable. In the same change, buffer.py removed the _load_segment_data max_segment_spans check that previously logged and skipped oversized segments, so that safety signal is gone as well. Note the hardcoded 1000 here also disagrees with SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (default 1001), which is now configurable but completely unused. Net effect: spans in large segments are discarded with no visibility, and the documented config limit is ignored; at minimum an eviction metric and consistency with max_segment_spans are needed.

findings.title: Redirect resolution depth reduced from 10000 to 1000 without accounting for the removed limit comment
findings.body: The redirect-walk loop was lowered from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000` (and the explanatory comment about segment trees of depth 10k removed). This bounds how far a chain of parent_span_id redirects is followed when merging subsegments. For traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 the walk stops before reaching the true segment key, so the span is attached to an intermediate key and the segment can be flushed split/duplicated rather than merged into its root. If the intent was to bound work, it should at least be justified and ideally tied to max_segment_spans, not silently set to 1000.

findings.title: Eviction path and new optimized paginator have no tests
findings.body: None of the updated buffer tests insert more than a handful of spans, so the new zpopmin eviction branch in add-buffer.lua (span_count > 1000) is never exercised; a regression there would be invisible. Likewise there is no test covering OptimizedCursorPaginator or the organization audit-log optimized_pagination branch, which is why the datetime-key crash and negative-slice crash above are not caught. Tests should cover a segment exceeding 1000 spans (asserting eviction keeps the expected spans and emits a metric) and the new paginator, including datetime ordering and negative-offset cursors.
